Definition: a yoke (properly, for plowing), i.e. the frame of a loom
BiblicalUsage: mânôwr is a weaver's beam, the heavy frame of a loom, and it is also the yoke for ploughing. In 1 Samuel 17:7 the staff of Goliath's spear is like a weaver's beam, and in 2 Samuel 21:19 the brother of Goliath carries a spear of the same size. The word measures a giant by the loom he would dwarf.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe mânôwr shows me that even giants are measured against ordinary work, and that God delights in bringing down what looks too big to fall.
RelatedTopics: Victory; God's Power; Strength in weakness
